topic: whether students should be required to do community service
text:
Students should be required to do community service because it helps them grow as responsible citizens, builds useful skills, and strengthens the ties that bind our neighborhoods together. First, when young people spend time helping others, they learn that their actions have real effects on the world around them. A teenager who tutors a younger child sees how a little patience can improve a struggling student’s confidence, and that lesson stays with them long after the tutoring ends. This kind of personal experience is far more powerful than any textbook lesson about civic duty.
Second, community service gives students practical skills that classrooms rarely teach. Working at a food bank teaches organization and time‑management, while cleaning up a park develops teamwork and problem‑solving abilities. These experiences look good on college applications and résumés, showing future employers that the student can handle real‑world responsibilities. If service were optional, many students would skip it to focus on grades or sports, missing out on these valuable lessons.
Some argue that forcing service takes away a student’s freedom to choose how they spend their time. However, most schools already require certain activities—like homework and attendance—so adding a modest service hour does not create an unreasonable burden. Instead, it ensures that every student, regardless of background, gets the chance to contribute and benefit from the community. In the long run, a generation that has regularly helped others will be more empathetic, more engaged, and better prepared to tackle the challenges of tomorrow. For these reasons, community service should be a required part of every student’s education.
